The '''1957–58 season''' was '''[[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid Club de Fútbol]]'s''' [[List of Real Madrid CF seasons|55th season]] in existence and the club's [[La Liga records and statistics#All-time La Liga table|27th consecutive season]] in the top flight of Spanish football.

The season saw Real Madrid win the [[Double (association football)#Continental Double|continental double]], clinching the European Cup for the third time in a row and successfully defending the La Liga championship. By winning the league, Madrid secured their 6th Primera División title and equalled Barcelona and Athletic Bilbao for most title wins.

The team got agonizingly close to clinching its first ever [[Treble (association football)|treble]], only to be defeated by [[Athletic Bilbao|Atlético de Bilbao]] in the [[1958 Copa del Generalísimo Final|Copa del Generalísimo final]].

==Summary==
The club signed 1955–56 French league champion manager [[Luis Carniglia]] as its new head coach.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/players/madrid-coach.html|publisher= Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation|title= Real Madrid managers}}</ref> New arrivals for the team were goalkeeper [[Rogelio Domínguez]], a champion with Argentina at the 1957 Copa América,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.historiadeboca.com.ar/tecnicos/rogelio-antonio-dominguez/33/1974/1974/10/0/1490.html|title=Rogelio Antonio Domínguez – Trayectoria y Biografía de Entrenadores|access-date=30 August 2018|publisher=historiadeboca.com.ar|language=es}}</ref> and from [[Nacional de Montevideo]] Uruguayan defender [[José Emilio Santamaría]], who played at the [[1954 FIFA World Cup]] and brought attention due to his style of play.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://futbol.as.com/futbol/2016/09/05/seleccion/1473063867_226121.html|title=Los 11 jugadores nacidos fuera de España con más partidos|trans-title=The 11 players born outside of Spain with the most matches|work=[[Diario AS]]|language=es|date=5 September 2016|accessdate=28 December 2016}}</ref> These two signings were crucial to boost the defense of the team with an impressive 26 goals conceded during 30 matches in the Spanish league, helping also the offensive line wherein Alfredo Di Stéfano and his 19 goals clinched another league top scorer trophy, this time tied with [[Manuel Badenes]] (Real Valladolid) and [[Ricardo Alós]] (Valencia) .

The team, with an excellent balance in defense and offense, won its sixth [[1957–58 La Liga|Spanish league]] title, finishing 3 points above [[Atlético Madrid]] despite a bad row of results during the winter. Also, the squad clinched its third consecutive [[1957–58 European Cup|European Cup]] defeating [[A.C. Milan]] 3–2 after extra time at Heysel.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Simpson |first1=Paul |last2=Hesse-Lichtenberger |first2=Uli |date=October 2005 |title=50 Things You Never Knew About... The European Cup |journal=[[FourFourTwo]] |issue=134 |page=101 |location=Teddington |publisher=Haymarket Consumer |editor1-first=Hugh |editor1-last=Sleight |issn=1355-0276 }}</ref> After clinching the two trophies, Madrid's attention turned to the [[1958 Copa del Generalísimo|Copa del Generalísimo]] with hopes of becoming the first team in the world to clinch the [[Treble (association football)|continental treble]]. [[Real Sociedad]] was defeated convincingly to set up the [[1958 Copa del Generalísimo Final|final]] against [[Athletic Bilbao|Atlético de Bilbao]] at the Bernabéu. Playing at home in front of 100,000 spectators with the treble on the line, Madrid were shut down by Athletic, losing 0–2. Real Madrid continued its unlucky run of losing Copa finals. As of 2022, the club has never won a treble, with its next closest attempt coming [[1961–62 Real Madrid CF season|four years later]].
